page: Hetzner Cloud cpx12 is an entry-level virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor and an AMD EPYC processor. It features a single shared x86_64 vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz, backed by 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.95 GB per core, and 40 GB of local SSD storage. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware are included.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The single-core CPU performance is strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2999.88, placing it in the top 25 percent. However, because it is limited to a single shared vCPU, its multi-core performance is weak, scoring in the bottom 25 percent on stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory performance is constrained, with a PassMark memory score in the bottom 10 percent and a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 146.65 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks perform at average levels, with gzip compression reaching 24.66 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 12.27 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the cpx12 instance is its shared CPU allocation and limited memory capacity, which restrict its utility for concurrent or memory-intensive workloads. PassMark database operations and static web serving throughput both fall into the bottom 10 percent of benchmarks, indicating limitations for high-traffic hosting. However, the instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for lightweight, single-threaded applications. It is suited for basic utility scripts, small-scale development environments, lightweight single-threaded tasks, and low-demand background workers.
